notes:
## Launch mode is a delegator now, not a babysitter

A real 8-agent Launch run burned an entire cloud quota in 51 minutes — 3,346 model
requests, 95% of that day's traffic — and finished 2 of 8 tasks. Launch had copied
Orchestrate's doctrine but none of its machinery. This release ports the machinery.

### The engine merges finished work
When an agent finishes its turn, ChatOSS commits its worktree and merges its branch into
yours automatically, then hands the orchestrator the outcome. No more model round-trip
per merge, and no more reading a transcript to decide whether work deserves merging. The
orchestrator resolves conflicts and runs your tests once over the merged batch. Merges are
serialized, the worktree is kept so agents stay drivable, and a wait doesn't return until
the merge has landed — "finished" now means "finished and merged".

### Sub-agents never stop to ask permission
They launch in auto mode. Previously they auto-approved *edits* but still asked before
every shell command — and a read-only investigation is nothing but shell commands. Two
agents in that run froze on an unanswered `rg` approval for 46+ minutes while the app
reported them as finished; one approval cost another agent 21 minutes of its 32-minute
life. OpenCode, which takes no permission flag, now gets a real `permission` block in its
generated config.

### The app can finally see an approval dialog
Claude Code's permission prompt was invisible to the app for three separate reasons, so
95 and 81 real dialogs on two agents were detected zero times — and because "is it
waiting?" was derived from that detection, every miss read as *turn complete*. Fixed and
regression-tested against byte-exact captures of the real screens: 176/176 frames now
classify as blocked. A dialog the app can't parse is still reported as blocked, never idle.

### The proxy stopped lying to the CLIs
- **Token usage was always zero.** Every Claude Code usage record and all 405 of Codex's
  token events read 0, so no CLI could see its own context growing — which is why Codex ran
  a single 37-minute turn straight into "prompt too long" instead of compacting. Real input
  and cached counts are now forwarded.
- **A fatal 400 arrived as a retryable 502.** Codex re-sent a 1,049,269-token prompt ~71
  times with no backoff. Real status codes are forwarded now, and a context overflow is
  always a 400.
- **No context window was advertised**, so Codex guessed 258,400 and overflowed near 1M.
  `/v1/models` and codex's model catalog now carry the real number, sourced from Ollama and
  omitted when unknown.
- A CLI's own sub-agent tool asked for a vendor model id and got a 404 — one such call died
  in 6 seconds, after which its parent polled the dead sub-agent 275 times over 39 minutes.
  Those now resolve to a live launch's model.

### Also
- Quiet now means the screen stopped changing, not that bytes stopped arriving — a TUI that
  repaints its footer had kept a finished agent unmergeable for 31 of its 39 minutes.
- Fatal errors (400, context overflow, retry loops) are recognized; the benign
  "model metadata not found" boot warning no longer masquerades as one. A context overflow
  triggers a single automatic compaction attempt.
- The orchestrator gets far less of each agent's screen, and read-only investigation while
  agents run is gated the same way Orchestrate gates it.
- Every task now carries an output contract: finish by committing, because the commit
  message is the only report that outlives the terminal.
- Abandoned agents no longer leak git worktrees.
- A hung Ollama daemon can no longer hang the `chatoss launch` command forever.
